question: Will a turn limit of 12 change how many runs pass?

options.text: Yes. Runs that hit the limit fail, so fewer runs pass.
options.why: Tempting. A limit looks like a failure, but a run that fixed the bug before the limit still passes.

options.text: No. The same runs pass, and the runs that loop stop sooner and cost less.
options.why: Right. The limit stops the loop, not the fix. Every run that passed before still passes.

options.text: Yes, and the new board passes every run, because the model has to finish.
options.why: Tempting. A limit does not make the model finish; it only ends the run.

outcome: The same runs pass on both boards. The looping runs stop at the limit instead of running on.

question: Which board ends more runs with a false done?

options.text: The old board. Its runs say done, nothing checks the claim, and the harness takes the word.
options.why: Right. With no verify gate, a done claim ends the run, even when the checks fail.

options.text: The new board. The verify gate adds more ways for a run to end wrong.
options.why: Tempting. The gate adds a check, not a new way to fail; it sends the run back when the checks fail.

options.text: Neither. A false done needs a model that lies.
options.why: Tempting. A false done is a claim the harness did not check. The model does not need to lie for it to happen.

outcome: The old board ends runs done with failing checks. The new board sends each run back to fix the work.

question: A turn limit stops a run before the next model call. Which wire is it on?

options.text: Control plane: it shapes the prompt the model sees.
options.why: Tempting. The prompt is built on the control wire, but a turn limit does not change it.

options.text: Loop and state: a guard that runs before each turn.
options.why: Right. The loop wire checks the guards before every new turn, and the turn limit is one of them.

options.text: Permissions: it decides which tools may run.
options.why: Tempting. Permissions decide each tool call. A turn limit counts turns, not calls.

options.text: Verification: it checks the work when the model says done.
options.why: Tempting. The verify gate checks done claims. The turn limit does not look at the work.
